📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, proposal a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

Starting today, Google announced, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

Recent findings suggest that once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response mentioned, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

Recent findings suggest that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Upcoming York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Recent findings suggest that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic concerns that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

It has been revealed that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

It has been revealed that reddit is an online forum where people share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several owners suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason.
  • It has been revealed that from protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without.
  • Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research indicates thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

It has been revealed that from protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

Sources indicate that smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you fresh locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

Say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

Video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one demonstrates up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

Sources indicate that these advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

Recent findings suggest that package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

Where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

These lights also give you phone app controls, which is more important than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

If you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

Gen Z is the least interested in AI at work – and it’s not even close

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.
  • Sources indicate that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found.
  • Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

Sources indicate that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

“Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” noted Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

In a recent development, around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

It’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

“We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster noted.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you’ve been thinking about buying an electric bike, scooter or electric unicycle, Black Friday and Cyber Monday are bringing some good opportunities to save. Segway, Apollo, Inmotion and several other manufacturers have marked down their rides, with discounts ranging from $100 to more than $1,000.

It has been revealed that I’ve had several of these models in-house for testing, from everyday commuters to bikes capable of carrying passengers and cargo. Some also offer features riders will appreciate, including automatic lighting, turn signals, Apple Find My support and rear-approach detection.

Industry observers note that saving money shouldn’t mean compromising on safety. That’s why I’m focusing on models with UL-certified electrical systems, specifically UL 2849 for e-bikes and UL 2272 for electric scooters and unicycles. Read more about battery safety and proper charging.With all of that in mind, here are the Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals worth checking out.

Sources indicate that the Segway Myon is one of the newer commuter e-bikes I’ve tried. It has a 500-watt motor, 85 Newton-meter of torque and pedal assistance up to 28 miles per hour. There’s also Apple Find My support, automatic lighting and Segway’s AirLock system, which can unlock the bike as you approach. You can also add the optional Rearview Radar for $100 to receive alerts about vehicles approaching from behind.

At $400 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for an everyday commuter with some useful technology built in.

Recent findings suggest that the Segway Muxi Pro is designed for carrying passengers and cargo, and I’ve been testing its practicality for everyday family use, including transporting my young son. The bike has automatic lighting, integrated turn signals and Apple Find My support, which can help locate the bike if it goes missing. It also includes the $100 Rearview Radar option.

The Muxi is an interesting alternative for errands and shorter trips where you might otherwise grab the car.

The Segway Xyber Air is another Segway I’ve tested, but this one is more about recreational riding than commuting or hauling groceries. Its moto-inspired design gives it a different look from your typical e-bike, and it supports Apple Find My, adding another layer of security when it’s parked.

Segway has additional deals on the Xafari and Xyber, with advertised savings reaching $1,300.

Shop all Segway Black Friday deals.

Regular price: $3,999 | Free charger valued at $259.

It has been revealed that the Aventon Current ADV isn’t discounted, but Aventon is including a fast charger valued at $259. I’ve tested this full-suspension electric mountain bike in-house. It has a mid-drive motor producing up to 120Nm of torque and a claimed maximum range of 105 miles. It also offers GPS-based security features, including location tracking and an alarm system. Even though it’s an e-mountain bike, I love how it handles Upcoming York’s bumpy streets.

Aventon has additional discounts of up to $200 on select Aventure, Level and Pace models.

Shop all Aventon Black Friday deals.

In a recent development, the Apollo Dash is aimed at first-time scooter riders who want something practical without spending a fortune. It weighs 43 pounds, folds in about three seconds and has a claimed range of up to 25 miles. It also supports Apple Find My, a useful feature if your scooter ever goes missing.

Recent findings suggest that I have the Dash in-house, but since I’m above its rated rider weight, my son and partner are handling the riding portion of the testing under my guidance. I’ll have more to share in a full hands-on review.

The Apollo Go Stellar offers a step up in performance with dual motors, a top speed of up to 32 mph and a claimed range of 38 miles. At 55 pounds, it’s heavier than the Dash but adds dual-spring suspension and Apple Find My support. It’s another scooter on my testing list.

Industry observers note that for riders looking for considerably more power, the Apollo Phantom 2.0 has dual motors, a top speed of up to 44 mph and a claimed range of 50 miles. It also features regenerative braking, dual-spring suspension, an IP66 water-resistance rating and Apple Find My support.

At 102 pounds, however, this isn’t a scooter you’ll want to carry up several flights of stairs.

Apollo also has discounts on its City lineup and higher-performance Phantom Stellar.

In a recent development, the Segway Max G3 Plus is another scooter we’ve had in-house. It has a claimed range of up to 56 miles, front and rear hydraulic suspension, 11-inch self-sealing tires, disc brakes and integrated turn signals. It also has Segway’s traction control system and electronic braking assistance.

Industry observers note that at $500 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for something with more performance and comfort than a basic commuter scooter. I’ll have more to share about my experience with it in an upcoming hands-on review.

According to recent reports, the Vmax VX2 Hub is one of the more powerful single-motor scooters we’ve tested, with 1,900 watts of peak power and an advertised top speed of 34 mph. What impressed me was how well it handled my weight, especially considering its relatively modest size. At $640 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a compact scooter with some serious power.

The Vmax VX2 Lite is another scooter on my review list. It’s a more affordable alternative to the Hub, and at $460 off, it could be worth checking out if you don’t need the Hub’s additional performance. I’ll have more to share once I’ve had a chance to test it.

Industry observers note that the Inmotion V9 is one of the more beginner-friendly electric unicycles I’ve reviewed. It has built-in cellular connectivity, allowing you to track its location if it goes missing, along with suspension for a more comfortable ride. It’s also UL 2272 certified, an crucial consideration when bringing a lithium-ion-powered ride into your home.

At $500 off, it’s an appealing option for anyone looking to get into electric unicycles without spending a fortune.

Shop Inmotion’s Black Friday deals.

If none of these models fit your needs, there are a few other sales worth checking out.

Super73 has discounts on select models, including the Z Miami Core and S2 Laguna, both priced at $1,895. Its sale runs through Dec. 2.

According to recent reports, velotric is offering savings of up to $700 on select e-bikes, including the Summit 1, advertised at $1,299. The Nomad 2 and folding Fold 1 Plus are also discounted.

Juiced Bikes has marked down several models in its Scrambler lineup for Black Friday. The Scrambler Mini starts at $949, down from $1,164, while the Scrambler Hardtail is $1,599 (save $445) and the Full Suspension is $1,799 (save $445). If you’re looking for more range, the dual-battery Hardtail is $1,899, down from $2,344.

Shop Juiced Bikes Black Friday deals.

Segway also has discounts on several other scooters, including the Max G2 for $598.48, ZT3 Pro for $790 and E3 Pro for $500.

Many of the manufacturers featured here have additional Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals across their product lines. I wanted to spotlight the bikes, scooters and electric unicycles we’ve had or presently have in-house because we’ve actually spent time with them. There are other products we’ve tested that could have made this list, too, but I wanted to give readers a useful selection rather than overwhelm them with every discounted model.

Industry observers note that don’t get too caught up in the discount. Make sure the bike, scooter or unicycle fits your needs, particularly when it comes to rider weight, range, portability and storage. Manufacturers’ range estimates are generally based on favorable conditions, and your actual mileage will vary depending on weight, speed, hills and temperature.

It has been revealed that apple Find My and other tracking systems can help locate a missing ride, but they’re no substitute for a good physical lock. And when it comes to battery safety, look for the appropriate UL certification, use the manufacturer-approved charger and never charge your bike or scooter where it blocks your exit.

Most of these deals run through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, although some promotions continue into December. Prices and availability can change.

You can turn Claude artifacts into Windows and Mac apps now – here’s how

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer.
  • Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.
  • Industry observers note that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Industry observers note that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks people do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

Recent findings suggest that “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic stated.

Artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they update automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free users.

Anthropic remarked the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

Recent findings suggest that also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

In a recent development, the update clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

“If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic stated.

Claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

Recent findings suggest that first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid prepares, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

It has been revealed that full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic said, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and upgrade the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

“Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the company said.

For Claude Enterprise plans, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

What Are Repositioning Cruises?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

According to recent reports, one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

In a recent development, just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a newly introduced region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit key sites when off the ship.

Sources indicate that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

In a recent development, for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy indicates, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Recent findings suggest that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

According to recent reports, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

Industry observers note that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Latest York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

In a recent development, if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and New England before reaching the Big Apple.

Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching Fresh York.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix race, some of those views were captured with iPhone Pro phones and transmitted in real time over T-Mobile’s 5G network.

According to recent reports, using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. In May, Apple broadcast a Major League Soccer game shot with iPhones strapped to professional lenses, following it up with a Major League Baseball game in September using its own camera hardware,.

According to recent reports, but compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the race track snakes 3.9 miles through the city’s downtown core. Its route includes the famed Strip (South Las Vegas Boulevard), where most of the big hotels are.

“We control everything on baseball, so we can do whatever we want there,” said Royce Dickerson, executive producer of live sports at Apple TV. “We did 14 iPhones on top of our normal camera complement” during the baseball broadcast. He noted that 10 of those were connected via T-Mobile’s 5G wireless network.

Recent findings suggest that but integrating iPhone cameras into an F1 broadcast, even for the sport’s US broadcaster, is more of a challenge. “I’ve been doing TV production for 20-plus years,” mentioned Dickerson, “and the scale of their operation is unlike anything I’ve seen before.”.

In a recent development, because F1 has agreements with other camera partners, Dickerson did not specify how many iPhones were set up around the track. Neither Apple nor T-Mobile explained where the iPhones were placed in order to capture the speedy F1 vehicles racing around the Vegas Strip. I suspect they were likely deployed in more conventional environments for smartphone cameras, like the team garages and roving to catch celebrities in the paddock area and in the stands, though the iPhone setups wirelessly broadcasting footage at earlier sporting events means they could be easily placed in many locations on and above the streets.

“You really have to work hard to earn the fans’ attention [and] that viewing experience,” mentioned Dickerson. “How are you getting your fans closer to their favorite athlete, to their favorite driver, to their team, to the personalities that surround the sport?”.

Recent findings suggest that in the T-Mobile zone at the Sphere – an area sponsored by the carrier and open to T-Mobile customers – at least 10 iPhone cameras were used to cover a stage where concerts played between events. That number is based on a diagram shared during a tour of T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer, where the company’s event coordinators stay on top of things like crowd movements and line lengths.

Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast, media and race operations at Formula 1, sees the combination of multiple cameras streaming wirelessly over 5G as an essential component to the Las Vegas race.

According to recent reports, “If we just did cameras at a low level, the fences and track, we haven’t done a very good job,” remarked Locke. “How can we open up stages, concerts and all of the activities? Each race has a real kind of personality to it. You can only [capture that personality] with huge amounts of cameras, huge amounts of technology.”.

According to recent reports, if Apple is using iPhones to record live sports, are they recording any of that footage using spatial video for viewing in the Vision Pro? Imagine getting a track-level view of a group of Formula 1 cars speeding past at 200 miles per hour with Apple’s depth effect. “[There’s] nothing at this time I can say about it,” said Dickerson.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 12:56PM EST.
  • According to recent reports, the digital advertising landscape is evolving rapidly, forcing investors to choose between specialized platforms.
  • Recent findings suggest that appLovin focuses on high-performance mobile app marketing, while Magnite operates as a sell-side platform connecting publishers with advertisers across connected TV and digital audio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 12:56PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than AppLovin ›.

According to recent reports, the digital advertising landscape is evolving rapidly, forcing investors to choose between specialized platforms. Should you bet on AppLovin (APP +5.35%) or Magnite (MGNI +2.42%) for your long-term portfolio growth?

Recent findings suggest that appLovin focuses on high-performance mobile app marketing, while Magnite operates as a sell-side platform connecting publishers with advertisers across connected TV and digital audio. Both companies benefit from the shift toward programmatic advertising, where software automates the buying and selling of digital ad space to reach specific audiences more efficiently.

Recent findings suggest that appLovin provides a marketing platform designed to help businesses advertise and measure their performance, primarily within the mobile gaming sector. The firm utilizes proprietary technology to power major mobile games and is right now expanding its reach into broader consumer brands. It maintains strategic relationships with major industry players like Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), Meta Platforms, Amazon (AMZN +3.96%), and Unity Software (U +4.27%), though it often competes with these same entities.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, AppLovin's revenue reached $7.6 billion--a 57.8% increase year-over-year on a continuing operations basis (excluding the divested Apps business). Net income was $5.0 billion, yielding a 65.9% net margin (the share of sales kept as profit after all expenses).

As of December 2025, its current ratio was 3.3x (over three times more current assets than short-term liabilities) and its debt-to-equity ratio was 1.7x (total debt relative to shareholder equity). Full-year 2025 free cash flow reached $3.95 billion after operating costs and capital expenditures.

Magnite operates as an independent sell-side platform, helping digital publishers monetize their content across connected TV, online video, and mobile displays. By serving as a bridge between media owners and ad buyers, the manufacturer facilitates ad placements in approximately 190 countries worldwide. It has established key partnerships with organizations like LG Ad Solutions and recently began working with OpenAI to integrate ad placements within advanced technology environments among communication stocks.

It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $766.7 million, growing by roughly 9.1% over the previous twelve-month period. The company reported net income of approximately $180.8 million, leading to a net margin of close to 23.6%. While revenue growth is more moderate than its peer, the positive net margin indicates the company is successfully converting a portion of its sales into actual profit.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.7x, suggesting a conservative level of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio stands at approximately 1.0x, indicating that current assets, such as cash and accounts receivable, roughly equal current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $165.6 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 32.5% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

AppLovin faces risks related to its heavy revenue concentration within the mobile app and gaming ecosystem. The company relies heavily on third-party distribution platforms like the Apple (AAPL +0.83%) App Store and Google Play Store, meaning changes to their rules can impact performance. Additionally, evolving privacy regulations such as the GDPR and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on intellectual property rights create ongoing uncertainty for its business model.

Magnite is significantly dependent on advertising spend within the connected TV market, which could be impacted if programmatic auction adoption slows. The company also deals with high customer concentration, as two buyers accounted for approximately 44% of its revenue in 2025. Furthermore, it faces intense competitive pressure from larger participants like The Trade Desk (TTD +2.48%) and PubMatic (PUBM +3.18%) while navigating a complex legal landscape involving litigation against major tech firms.

While AppLovin carries a higher price relative to its sales, both companies trade at very similar valuations when considering their future earnings estimates.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with AppLovin. Advertisers are spending more on ads that deliver measurable results, and AppLovin's AI engine sits right in the middle of that, deciding which ad each person sees in mobile apps and, increasingly, online stores. And it's paying off in a significant way. Revenue is up 55% year over year, and about two-thirds of every sales dollar ends up as profit.

The tech giant isn't without baggage, though. It still leans heavily on mobile games, and it faces investor lawsuits and short-seller claims that it disputes. Still, I'm excited to see that its latest quarter beat the company's own targets by a wide margin.

Magnite is doing plenty right. It helps streaming services and publishers sell ad space, its streaming TV business is growing fast, and it earns a healthy profit. But it is a much smaller business growing more slowly, and a record midterm political-ad season gave last quarter a lift that is hard to repeat.

It has been revealed that appLovin, meanwhile, is growing much faster and has extraordinary profit margins, yet its stock isn't any pricier than Magnite's compared with the profits analysts expect. For long-term investors, an AI ad engine this profitable, at a similar price, makes AppLovin the better buy for 2027.

  • According to recent reports, the Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite latest cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.

According to recent reports, the Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner. / CNET/Ajay Kumar.

It has been revealed that the Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce. Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability.

At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.

Shark StainForce cleaning a stain off my carpet. / Ajay Kumar/CNET.

The Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains.

It works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots.

The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life.

In a recent development, the tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that said, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains.

I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

Here I am scrubbing away with the StainForce powered on. You can still see some stain, but it’s going away.

Sources indicate that the Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference shows in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

Industry observers note that the StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

Sources indicate that that proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

Recent findings suggest that what I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.

Industry observers note that if you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a massive and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lee Samaha – Nov 27, 2026 at 1:07PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vera Therapeutics ›.

Sources indicate that vera Therapeutics (VERA +16.14%) stock was up more than 16% at midday today, but the increase didn't stem from any direct news from the organization. Instead, the news came from a much larger company, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, (VRTX -5.24%) aiming to get a rival drug to Vera's Trutakna (atacicept) approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Recent findings suggest that vera's Trutakna is indicated for the treatment of primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) in adults. It received approval in the summer, and as you might imagine, a small biotechnology company like Vera, competing with a giant like Vertex with a $135 billion market cap, will push hard to establish Trutakna sales before Vertex can get its rival IgAN treatment drug, povetacicept, approved.

NASDAQ · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

Vertex's drug is a real threat, not least as it's taken once every four weeks as opposed to Trutakna's once-a-week dosing.

As such, the recent news that the FDA had issued an extension "to the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date for the Biologics License Application (BLA) for povetacicept for the treatment of IgA nephropathy (IgAN) by up to three months" reads like a shot in the arm for Vera's attempts to build sales.

Not only does it give Vera up to three months to build sales and get patients and physicians used to the treatment, but the fact that the extension was issued at all casts some doubt on ultimate approval.

Sources indicate that vertex's press release noted that the extension was due to an FDA information request, to which it promptly replied, prompting the FDA to require more time to review Vertex's submission. The sell-off in Vertex's stock may well be an overreaction to what could turn out to be merely a delay in approval. Still, that won't worry Vera too much, as it now has a few extra months to build Trutakna's market presence.

Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Recent findings suggest that the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

My point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Industry observers note that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

According to recent reports, mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

Sources indicate that strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

Industry observers note that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI highlighted wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

According to recent reports, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

Recent findings suggest that but back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

It has been revealed that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

Recent findings suggest that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a fresh home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
  • Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
  • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the firm like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Recent findings suggest that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and unveiled the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
  • According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
  • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

There are four main types of grants:.

Federal grants come from the federal government.

State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

Industry observers note that to receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

Sources indicate that federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

According to recent reports, some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

After you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

Sources indicate that most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal plan.

In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

In a recent development, grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

Some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

After your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment aims, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

According to recent reports, your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

According to recent reports, yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

Sources indicate that you don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

You withdrew from your program.

You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

It has been revealed that it depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

If you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

Industry observers note that grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

Recent findings suggest that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to latest inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Like I mentioned above, it's not totally obvious where mortgage rates will head next. Let's walk through the two scenarios.

Here's why rates could go up: This morning, we got October's Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, also known as PCE. It's the last measure of inflation to come out each month, but it's also the Federal Reserve's preferred metric, so PCE gets a lot of attention.

The stats came in mostly as predicted, though it's not like the predictions were good — inflation's been overly strong for a while. But the core year-over-year figure, which came in a tenth of a percent over predictions, could prove troublesome. Core PCE removes categories that can be extra volatile, so it's considered a measure that shows the underlying trend. In this case, the underlying trend is Not Good.

It has been revealed that it's already pretty much a lock that we'll see a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, because yes, raising the federal funds rate is the Fed's main tool for taming inflation. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but a rate-hiking cycle from the central bankers definitely keeps upward pressure on borrowing costs.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, here's why that same inflation data could help rates go down: Over the past several days, we've watched the stock market go on a wild ride, with the Anthropic IPO and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Yesterday, things weren't looking good for tech stocks, and these inflation numbers could make it even worse.

Sources indicate that the amount that tech companies have borrowed to fund AI buildout is a significant concern for investors, since companies will have to cover those costs before investors see any profits. It's already a big task, and if everything costs more thanks to inflation, it's that much harder.

This AI-related anxiety is rough on the stock market, but it's been a boon for Treasury bonds. More demand for bonds pushes up bond prices, which brings down bond yields (basically, the return investors get on a bond). Mortgage rates for 30-year loans are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, so here's why you care about all of this: Lower Treasury yields means lower mortgage rates, too. If investors keep stressing about inflation eating into tech profits, we could see mortgage rates continue to move lower.

That was a lot of info on inflation, but inflation's not the only major metric influencing rates.

Recent findings suggest that let's back up for a second. The Federal Reserve tries to keep the economy steady by focusing on two key goals, often referred to as the Fed's dual mandate. One side is price stability — keeping inflation reasonable. The other is maximum employment, meaning those who want to work are able to find jobs.

Sources indicate that next week we'll shift our focus to the employment side of the Federal Reserve's mandate, because the first week of the month is always all about employment data. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, we'll kick things off with the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). JOLTS can tip us off to trends in the labor market; stuff like whether folks are leaving jobs voluntarily or if companies have openings that are going unfilled.

On Wednesday, payroll firm ADP will release its monthly employment stats. ADP is looking at its own payroll data to get an idea of how the job market is growing or contracting. The numbers don't include the public sector, but ADP often provides a preview of how the jobs report will go.

It has been revealed that the Employment Situation Summary, better known as the jobs report, drops on Friday. This is the big one, since it tells us the nation's unemployment rate. The jobs report's other major stat is, similar to ADP, how many jobs the economy added or lost in the previous month. Unlike ADP though, the jobs report is inclusive of everybody in the public and private sectors.

According to recent reports, lately the labor market's been looking super healthy, which is great news for the economy but less positive for mortgage rates. When hiring's strong, the Fed can feel safer raising the federal funds rate (that's the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers adjust). Higher rates tend to discourage businesses from borrowing and expanding, so if the job market's on shaky footing, the central bankers are going to be cautious about raising the benchmark rate.

Sources indicate that what we're seeing now though, where inflation is clearly the problem and employment's just fine, is a recipe for higher rates. Again, the Fed doesn't control mortgage rates, but the central bank being in rate-hike mode puts upward pressure on mortgage rates.

According to recent reports, if we were to see employment falter in this latest round of numbers, it still probably wouldn't change the Fed's initiative. That would be one poor month for the labor market versus months upon months of inflation running rampant — so yeah, they'll keep an eye on jobs, but inflation's still the scourge.

Our most likely source of lower mortgage rates in the short term is what I described above; investors who are leery of inflation and the promise of AI looking to the safe harbor of the bond market.

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.55% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, VSE (VSEC +3.08%) confirmed record quarterly revenue of $541 million and raised its full-year outlook. For long-term investors, the organization is converting aviation aftermarket demand into expanding profit margins and stronger cash generation. Three takeaways from management's comments highlight the key drivers.

VSE expanded its profit margins by combining a greater mix of higher-margin product and repair activity with cost synergies from recent acquisitions. Expanding adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) margins gives the company more cash to reinvest into its maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) network.

Sources indicate that management acquired Atech Turbine Components to add OEM-approved (original equipment manufacturer) repairs covering more than 300 part numbers to its portfolio. Owning proprietary intellectual property (IP) gives the business greater pricing power and insulates margins compared to standard component distribution.

Sources indicate that generating $47 million in quarterly free cash flow--cash left over after operating expenses and capital investments--helped VSE lower its adjusted net leverage ratio to 2.3 times debt to EBITDA. Stronger cash flow gives management flexibility to pay down debt from past acquisitions while continuing to fund organic repair expansion.

It has been revealed that high fleet utilization and constrained fresh aircraft deliveries support steady repair volume, while exclusive distribution agreements protect pricing discipline. Operations teams are watching supply chain lead times to maintain shop throughput.

Combining proprietary repair IP with disciplined debt reduction positions the firm to expand margins across commercial and general aviation.
